thread:
Noah (PM): dropping a compact timeline experiment — goal: surface more versions on small widths without losing canary clarity. Figma: https://figma.com/file/compact-rollouts. Two approaches in mock: 'inline microcopy' and 'token legend'. Thoughts?

Priya - Design: Inline microcopy keeps context but gets noisy with 3+ variants. Token legend reduces clutter but risks extra cognitive load. In the mock I added tiny numbered tokens (1,2,3) inside the strip and a persistent legend below on hover/click.

Ethan (frontend): Implementation notes: token legend is easy visually but we must keep the DOM order semantically meaningful. I'm worried about hover-only legends; mobile needs tap-to-open. Also watch for layout shifts when legend appears.

Marta (a11y): Accessibility rules: don't hide critical information behind hover. If tokens are used, each token must have an accessible name like \"Variant 1: canary 5 percent\". Provide a toggle to expand the legend with role=\"button\" and aria-expanded. Example: <button aria-expanded=\"false\" aria-controls=\"legend-1\">Legend</button>.

Lina (SRE): Operationally, engineers scanning timelines expect to see exact percentages quickly. If we hide numbers, we should surface them on keyboard focus and in the aria-label. Also consider a compact focus mode that temporarily expands details for scanning.

Priya - Design: Copy nits: instead of \"Rollback\" propose \"Revert to last stable\" in the CTA. For the inline microcopy I used \"5% canary\" which reads better at a glance. For the legend header: \"Variants in this rollout\" and include small timestamps.

Ethan (frontend): For the modal confirm flow we'll add data-experiment=\"revert-cta-token\" so product can flip the label client-side. We'll also implement a focus trap using the modal library and ensure ESC cancels.

Marta (a11y): Modal should be role=\"alertdialog\" and set aria-modal=\"true\". On confirm, announce via aria-live: \"Deployment reverted to v78. Traffic at 100 percent.\" Return focus to the timeline control and avoid stealing focus on ephemeral toasts.

Noah (PM): Quick UX test plan: recruit 6 folks (mix of SRE/product) and ask them to find canary percent and initiate a revert. Track time-to-action and errors. A/B test token legend vs inline microcopy.

Priya - Design: UI tweaks: add subtle chevrons for expandable tokens, ensure tokens have at least 12px hit area, and add a subtle outline on focus. Color usage: use distinct hues but also include textual state (Live/Canary) to avoid color-only cues.

Ethan (frontend): CSS detail: prefer transform animations for perf; respect prefers-reduced-motion. For legend we can lazy-render content to avoid heavy DOM on initial load.

Lina (SRE): Edge case: when multiple canaries overlap across regions, tokens collide. Suggest a collapsed stack state that shows "+2" with hover/expand to see each region. Also ensure audit logs list exact rollout diffs.

Marta (a11y): Additional checklist items: keyboard-only interaction with tokens, screen reader ordering (most recent first default), and aria-describedby linking token to timestamp and traffic percent. Provide example SR-friendly labels in PR.

deploy-bot: Canary started — Variant 1 at 5% — triggered by noah — ts:1860209901

Noah (PM): Action items: Priya to produce two updated mocks (token legend with persistent legend and inline microcopy with expanded focus mode); Ethan to prototype tabbable tokens + modal experiment flag; Marta to draft accessibility acceptance criteria and example SR labels; Lina to validate legend behavior with multi-region rollouts. Back on Monday for a short review. Thanks! :handshake:
